verses.1: I say, in my heart, I truly want to cry out in joy. I see nothing but good things, and yet, he is also unhappy.
verses.2: I said, “What a shameful thing to do! What joy is this that he does?”
verses.3: In my heart, I strive to act with wisdom. My heart always seeks wisdom and avoids foolishness. Until then, I will not see that this is good for human beings, who live under the heavens for their entire lives.
verses.4: I have built houses for myself; I have planted trees for me.
verses.5: I planted gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them.
verses.6: I made a pond of water, so that I could use it to water a forest full of trees.
verses.7: I bought servants and wives, and I also had many sheep and cattle. All these were things that I had before I went to Jerusalem.
verses.8: I also obtained gold and silver, as well as royal garments. I made for myself beautiful dresses and jewelry. These were gifts from the people of the land.
verses.9: And I grew up, and I became more mature from everything that happened to me in Jerusalem. Even my wisdom stood with me.
verses.10: And everything that they asked me to do, I did without any hesitation. I didn’t delay my heart from any joy, because my heart was happy despite all the hardships I faced. And that became part of all my hardships.
verses.11: And I turned my attention to all the things that my hands had done, and to the hard work I had put in to accomplish them. But now, everything is darkness and evil. There’s no hope under the sun.
verses.12: And I turned my face towards wisdom and foolishness. What kind of person can come after a king who has already done such evil things?
verses.13: And I saw that there is more wisdom than foolishness, just as light is more than darkness.
verses.14: The wise man has wise eyes, while the foolish person walks in darkness. I also know that one person can bring all of them to life.
verses.15: And I said, “In my heart, I am like a fool. Yet I still value wisdom. Why should I be wise? I’ll just speak from my heart—even though that too is worthless.”
verses.16: For the wise man’s memory is forgotten forever by the foolish. In the days to come, everything will be forgotten. How can the wise man live with the foolish?
verses.17: And I hated all those living things, because the actions that took place under the sun were all evil and full of corruption.
verses.18: And I rejoice over all my efforts that I have put into working under the sunlight, so that people may be able to follow in my footsteps.
verses.19: And who can tell whether a wise man will become a fool, or whether someone else will rule over all the efforts I’ve made and all the wisdom I’ve accumulated under the sun… Even so, it’s still dark.
verses.20: And I am ashamed of my heart, for all the hard work I’ve done under the sun.
verses.21: For there is a person who has worked hard with wisdom, knowledge, and diligence. But for those who have not worked hard in this way, they will also be given their share of darkness and great evil.
verses.22: For man is like a worker under the sun; he labors under all his toil and suffering.
verses.23: For all his days are filled with pain and anger. Even at night, his heart cannot rest in peace. This is the curse that befell him.
verses.24: There is nothing good in a person who eats and drinks, yet still sees nothing good in himself. Even in his work, I see that it’s all from God.
verses.25: For who will eat and who will drink away from me?
verses.26: For to a person who is good in front of him, wisdom and knowledge are given; but to the wicked, they are given troubles and difficulties. This is also a sign that there is darkness and evil in their hearts.
